sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Button style rules
sections.what: Defines the base button style and the named looks: primary, secondary, glass, ghost, outline, destructive and emerald. Also defines four sizes: small, medium, large and icon. Sets the default to primary and medium.
sections.why: Likely reason: named styles keep buttons consistent, so a screen only has to name the style it wants.
sections.watch_out: Styles are picked by name, so a misspelled name produces a button with no look at all.

sections.name: ButtonProps
sections.title: Button component and loading spinner
sections.what: Draws the button with a slight press and hover animation. Shows a spinning icon before the label while loading. Passes every other setting through to the real button element.
sections.why: Likely reason: a single component keeps the press effect and loading display identical across screens.
sections.watch_out: Loading shows a spinner but does not disable the button, so a caller that does not also disable it can trigger the action twice.

summary: The shared button used across the app, with named styles, sizes and a loading spinner.
purpose: Give every button the same look and behavior, so screens only choose a style name.
why: Likely reason: one shared button keeps animation, spacing and loading display consistent everywhere.
how: 1. Builds the style from the chosen look and size, defaulting to primary and medium. 2. Wraps the button in an animated element that presses in slightly. 3. Shows a spinner in front of the label if loading. 4. Passes all other settings through to the real button.
inputs: Look name, size name, loading flag, label content, extra class names, and any normal button settings such as click handlers and disabled.
outputs: A styled button on screen. Clicks go to whatever handler the caller provides.
risks: Loading shows a spinner but does not disable the button, so repeated clicks can still fire the action. A misspelled look or size name gives a button with no style.
debug: If a button looks plain, check the look and size names against the lists in this file. If a loading button still accepts clicks, the caller needs to disable it. If animation looks wrong, check the motion library version.
